atlas.why: pale uprights receding into a muted blue-green field: depth and murk for the sugar-cube towers

takes.seen: 0-2.5 s cockpit matches the master (six-bolt port with chip, ballast slot, chalk chart, toggle, amber lamp, dent) with sugar-cube towers rising in the port; a tail fan and a bit of blue head sit at the lower right edge beside the toggle and the lamp wash brightens by 1.7 s; 3-5 s push-in, two reels on the pebbles and tape ribbons waving up between the towers, the ribbons glint cranberry red at about 3.7-4.5 s then go brown, a speckled trout holds among the towers and a faint turkey reflection sits lower right on the glass; by 6.3 s the standing ribbons are gone and a strip of tape lies on the bed between the reels (the rewind); cut between 6.3 and 7.0 s to the outside view: riveted metal tin, Turkey behind the amber port, two trout in the left foreground looking in

open: outside view (7-8 s) has no reel, no tape ribbon and no sugar towers: nothing is pulled taut to the hull, so Trout's two readings (rolling jukebox speaker / wire-chewer) are not staged; only Turkey's pair is supported
the tin does not visibly rock and the lamp pulse is not readable in the outside frames
Turkey's tail fan, not just a wing tip, enters at lower right and covers part of the right wall; the toggle stays visible but no wing is seen flipping it, only the lamp wash brightening
the cut across the glass lands late (after 6.3 s, not 5.5 s), leaving about 1.3 s outside
the reverse rule reads only as ribbons disappearing onto the bed; reels spinning backward cannot be confirmed from the frames
two trout outside instead of one; backward-falling bubbles not seen
the red glint lasts under a second, and the 'propeller snare' reading rests only on a loop near the glass
